Alex: quick heads-up — canary for customer 'atlas' showed a tail-latency spike + ~3% NaN tokens on long-context runs (~12k). rolled back canary, but we should investigate. logs show: RuntimeError: kernel produced NaN outputs (softmax overflow)
InfraBot: rollback executed for canary-456 -> stable-kernel-2026-03
Maria: thanks. do we have a repro? which kernel variant was selected by the selector?
Alex: repro local with the atlas prompt. selector chose flashx-fp8-optimized path due to batching heuristics (batch affinity + small per-request memory). microbench (local, same GPU):
```
flashx-fp8    seq=12k kv_reuse=0.7  p50=22ms  p99=450ms  NaN_rate=0.03
paged-fused-bf16 seq=12k kv_reuse=0.7 p50=28ms p99=320ms NaN_rate=0.00
fused-flash-bf16 seq=12k kv_reuse=0.7 p50=26ms p99=340ms NaN_rate=0.00
```
Tyler: interesting — NaNs only when kv_reuse > ~6k? also any pattern with temperature?
Alex: yes. NaNs surface when kv_coldstart is low and reuse ratio high. also higher temps (>=1.0) amplify logits so exp overflows. profiler points to softmax stage inside flashx_fp8_kernel.cu: exp(logits - max) producing inf because logits after qk_scale drift ~1e4. stack snippet: `softmax_forward -> compute_exp -> expf(x) -> INF`
Chen: sounds like fp8 accumulation / scaling mismatch. are we using per-head scaling constants? maybe a stale scale gets used after long kv runs. any changes in quant params recently?
Jamie: immediate mitigations: 1) clamp logits before exp (eg clamp(x, -40, +40)) 2) route these cases to bf16 softmax accumulation (more stable) 3) add an L2 check in kernel selector to prefer paged-fused when seq_len large. clamping is easy but may hide an upstream quant bug.
Maria: agree on fallback policy. proposal: if seq_len >= 8k and kv_reuse_ratio >= 0.6, prefer paged-fused-bf16 kernel. also add a fast NaN/Inf sample probe after kernel launch to trigger dynamic fallback.
Tyler: ran a quick compare: switching to bf16_paged_fused raises p50 22 -> 30ms but drops p99 450 -> 310ms and NaN_rate -> 0. looks acceptable for atlas SLA.
Alex: I'm prepping a PR with two changes: softmax clamp + kernel-selector rule + instrumentation to capture per-request inf_count. also adding a softmax-safeguard compile flag that forces fp32 accumulation for the reduce when enabled.
InfraBot: CI started for PR #4321 (alex/softmax-fallback).
Jamie: :thumbsup: add a unit test with synthetic logits [1e4, -1e4, 0] and verify no NaN and stable probs within eps, and a perf microbench comparing clamp vs full stable log-sum-exp path.
Chen: note: clamp reduces immediate risk but we should measure scaling drift over kv lifetime. add metrics: quant_scale_mean, quant_scale_std, and kv_accum_max every 1k tokens. if scale drift > threshold, trigger a maintenance alert to rebuild quant tables.
Maria: +1. also tag me on the nightly bench run after this PR lands. we need p50/p95/p99 and NaN_rate graphs.
Alex: will post EOD bench results. for now canary remains rolled back until PR merges and we validate. thanks team.
